message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Why it’s useful |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Quick, interactive, works from any shell that has the Cloud SDK installed. |
| **REST API (curl)** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Useful if you’re building a programmatic workflow or integrating with another system that can’t run the SDK. |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud calls its virtual‑machine service **Compute Engine**, not “EC2” (that’s AWS).  
> *The RTX A6000 GPU is available as `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> *You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, the Compute Engine API enabled, and the proper IAM permissions (`roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` or higher).  
> *GPU‑enabled instances require a **GPU‑compatible machine type** (e.g., `n1-standard-8`, `n1-highmem-8`, `n1-highcpu-8`).  
> *After the instance boots you’ll need to install the NVIDIA driver (the startup‑script below does that automatically).  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
  --zone="${ZONE}" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
  --tags="http-server,https-server" \
  --labels="env=dev,team=ai"
```

### `startup.sh` – Install NVIDIA driver & CUDA

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install prerequisites
apt-get install -y gnupg2 wget

# Add NVIDIA package repositories
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-1_amd64.deb
dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-1_amd64.deb
apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/7fa2af80.pub
apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit
apt-get install -y cuda-drivers
apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-2

# Clean up
apt-get clean
rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

> **Tip**: If you prefer a different CUDA version, change the URLs in `startup.sh` accordingly.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

> **Prerequisites**  
> *An OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
> *The `gcloud` CLI can generate one quickly: `gcloud auth print-access-token`.  
> *Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, and `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with your values.

```bash
# 1️⃣  Build the JSON payload
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y gnupg2 wget\nwget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin\nmv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600\nwget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-1_amd64.deb\ndpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-1_amd64.deb\napt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/7fa2af80.pub\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-drivers\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-12-2\napt-get clean\nrm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "labels": {
    "env": "dev",
    "team": "ai"
  }
}
EOF

# 2️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **What the JSON does**  
> *Creates a boot disk from the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family.*  
> *Adds one RTX A6000 GPU.*  
> *Runs a startup script that installs the NVIDIA driver and CUDA 12.2.*  
> *Attaches the instance to the default VPC network with an external IP.*  
> *Adds HTTP/HTTPS firewall tags and labels.*

---

## 3. Verify the Instance

Once the instance is running, you can check that the GPU is visible:

```bash
# SSH into the instance
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone="${ZONE}"

# Inside the VM
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version and CUDA capability.

---

## 4. Clean Up (Optional)

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone="${ZONE}" --quiet
```

---

### Quick Reference

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `gcloud compute instances create …` | Create instance via CLI |
| `gcloud auth print-access-token` | Get OAuth token |
| `curl -X POST …` | Create instance via REST |
| `nvidia-smi` | Verify GPU inside VM |
| `gcloud compute instances delete …` | Delete instance |

Feel free to copy/paste the snippets into your terminal or scripts. Let me know if you’d like help automating this in a CI/CD pipeline or adding additional configuration (e.g., custom firewall rules, persistent disks, or autoscaling).
